The paper does not report a blind-test classification accuracy for ternary bacterial mixtures.

The only blind-test result is in Section 3.6 (page 6). There, blind tests were run on four strains at unknown concentrations, and they "delivered 100% classification accuracy (Tables S9-S12)." That test concerns single strains at varying concentrations, not mixtures.

For the ternary mixtures (A + B + C at 1:1:1), Section 3.7 (page 7) reports only LDA score plots (Fig. 4d-f, Fig. S19b-f, Tables S16-S18) and says they "could also be effectively classified." No accuracy figure is given.
question: What classification accuracy did the blind tests achieve on the ternary bacterial mixtures?
